more.eyebrow: What makes it more than a log reader
more.h2: Your phone eats your limit too. Now you see it – on your desktop.
more.p: Many usage trackers read log files on your computer, so they only know what that one computer used. Claude Usage Monitor can ask Anthropic's server instead – and shows the real, account-wide number: everything you use in the phone app, in the browser, on another computer and in Claude Code counts, and you see it all in one place, on your desktop.

about.p: Claude Usage Monitor is a free, open-source desktop widget for Windows 10/11 and macOS that shows your Claude subscription's usage limits in real time – the five-hour session, the weekly limit and the per-model weekly limit, each with the time left until it resets. It stays on top of your other windows, so you can check your Claude usage without opening Settings → Usage and without a terminal.
about.p2: One app for both Windows and Mac. It covers everything that counts toward your plan – claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code, on all your devices. It is not the terminal tool “Claude Code Usage Monitor”: this one is a graphical panel with a tray icon, and needs no command line.
gl.1d: Claude's short-term usage limit. Your session-based limit resets every five hours. Anthropic calls it the “current session”; many users call it the 5-hour window or 5-hour limit.
gl.2d: A second cap on paid Claude plans that applies across all models and resets at a fixed time each week, assigned to your account. Weekly limits have been in effect since 28 August 2025.
gl.3d: A separate weekly cap for one specific model, listed on Claude's usage page next to the limit for all other models. The widget shows it as a third gauge for the model you choose.
gl.4d: The moment a limit goes back to 0%. The widget counts down to it. With claude.ai sign-in the exact time comes from Anthropic's server; with the local log it is an estimate.
gl.5d: How far you are ahead of or behind an evenly used week. “+12% vs pace” means you have used 12 percentage points more of your weekly limit than the share of the week that has passed.
gl.6d: How fast a limit is filling up right now – percent per hour for the session, percent per day for the week – and when it would reach 100% at that speed.
gl.7d: Optional pay-as-you-go usage after you reach your plan's limits, with a monthly spending cap. The widget shows whether it is switched on, the cap and what you have spent.
feat.h2: All your Claude usage limits. One glance.
feat.1d: Green, yellow, red. The panel changes colour long before you run out – with a countdown to the reset and an estimate of when you'd hit 100%.
feat.2d: The pace indicator tells you if your weekly limit is melting faster than the week passes – and projects where you'll end up.
feat.3d: Sign in through your own browser – like Claude Code does – and see usage from your phone, browser and every other computer too.
feat.4d: Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Claude Code, usage credits – every limit the server reports, plus this week's split between models.
feat.5d: A quiet notification at 70% and 90% (you choose), and when your limit resets. Nothing else, ever.
feat.7t: The whole week on one chart
feat.7d: Double-click the widget: both limits on one timeline – 6 hours, 24 hours or 7 days – with your weekly peak, daily average and an end-of-week projection that changes colour before you overshoot.
feat.6d: No telemetry, no analytics, no account with us. It talks only to Anthropic, only for your own numbers. Your sign-in token stays encrypted on your computer – Windows DPAPI or the macOS Keychain.
band1.p: No trial clock. No “Pro” upsell. No catch. Download it and it's yours.
tabs.h2: The details – when you want them.
tabs.p1:
• 5-hour session – current %, countdown to reset, burn rate (%/hour) and when it would fill up.
  • Weekly limit – current %, time to the weekly reset, daily rate and your pace vs. an even week.
  • Per-model weekly limit – a third gauge for the model you watch (Fable by default).
  • Plan badge – PRO, MAX 5×, MAX 20×, TEAM or ENTERPRISE.
  • History window – 6 h / 24 h / 7 days charts, weekly peak, daily average and an end-of-week projection.
  • Tray / menu-bar icon – your chosen percentage as a ring, details on hover.
tabs.p2:
1 · Local log default · no sign-in

Reads the usage log Claude Desktop already writes on your computer. Nothing is sent anywhere. Measures this computer only, refreshes about every 5 minutes.

2 · claude.ai all devices

The same browser sign-in Claude Code uses – no embedded browser, no password typed into the app. Exact reset times from the server, refreshed about every 2 minutes.
tabs.p3:
• No telemetry. The app has no analytics and never phones home – it only checks this site for a newer version.
  • Your token stays yours. Encrypted with Windows DPAPI, or stored in the macOS Keychain. Never in a plain file.
  • Conversations are never read. From local logs only the model name, token counts and timestamps are used.
  • Verified updates. HTTPS only, every download is checked against its SHA-256 before it is installed; on failure the old version comes back.
  • Open source. Don't trust – verify: the whole source is on GitHub under the MIT licence.

  • Alerts – warning and danger thresholds (70% / 90% by default), reset and stale-data notices.

faq.h2: Questions about Claude usage limits – short answers.
faq.q1: Is it really free? What's the catch?
faq.a1: Really free, and there is no catch. It's not a demo, not a trial and not a cut-down edition – this is the full and only version. No ads, no paid tier, no data collection. The source code is public under the MIT licence.
faq.q8: How do I check my Claude usage without opening Settings?
faq.a8: Install Claude Usage Monitor: it keeps your five-hour session, weekly limit and per-model limit on screen all the time, as a small always-on-top widget and as a percentage in the tray or menu bar. Claude's own numbers live under Settings → Usage; the widget shows the same limits without any clicking.
faq.q9: When do the Claude 5-hour session and the weekly limit reset?
faq.a9: The session-based limit resets every five hours. The weekly limit resets at a fixed time each week that Anthropic assigns to your account, so it differs from person to person. The widget shows a live countdown to both resets – with claude.ai sign-in it uses the exact times from Anthropic's server.
faq.q10: Does Claude Code usage count toward my claude.ai limit?
faq.a10: Yes. According to Anthropic, usage on claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code counts toward the same usage limit. That is why the widget's claude.ai mode shows one number for all your devices and apps, not only for the computer it runs on.
faq.q11: Is this the same as “Claude Code Usage Monitor”?
faq.a11: No. “Claude Code Usage Monitor” is a separate, terminal-based tool by another author. Claude Usage Monitor by Vidovics Gábor is a graphical desktop widget for Windows and macOS with a tray icon, themes and alerts, and it needs no command line.
faq.q2: Is this an official Anthropic product?
faq.a2: No. It's an independent community tool made by Vidovics Gábor. It is not affiliated with Anthropic. “Claude” is a trademark of Anthropic, PBC.
faq.q3: Do I have to give it my password?
faq.a3: Never. Without signing in it reads Claude Desktop's local log. If you want all devices, you sign in on claude.ai in your own browser – the app never sees your password.
faq.q4: Windows warns me when I run it. Why?
faq.a4: Because the app isn't code-signed (certificates cost money; the app is free). Click More info → Run anyway. You can verify the download with its SHA-256 checksum, and read the source on GitHub.
faq.a5: macOS 12 or newer. The download card above always shows which processor the current build is for. The macOS version is new – feedback is very welcome.
faq.a6: The app checks this site a few times a day. When there's a new version it tells you; one click downloads, verifies and installs it, then restarts. You can switch this off.
faq.a7: Windows: Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Claude Usage Monitor → Uninstall. macOS: drag the app to the Bin. That's all.
